code_actions.rationale: Progress notes and ID consult document ventilator-associated pneumonia developing after intubation (VAP suspected on hospital day 6) with Pseudomonas identified and treated (ev_0006, ev_0002, ev_0005). Governing VAP policy classifies J95.851 as MCC and requires POA = N when VAP develops during admission (pol_001). The originally billed POA=Y and CC tier are incorrect and are corrected here.

Although CRRT/HD was initiated (ev_0007), the problem list and discharge summary document renal recovery and that hemodialysis was discontinued (ev_0009, ev_0005). Dependence on dialysis (Z99.2) should be removed because it had resolved by discharge.

Cardiology describes troponin elevation and arrhythmia as secondary to sepsis/catecholamines and does not diagnose NSTEMI; discharge summary does not list NSTEMI (ev_0008, ev_0005). No provider-authored NSTEMI diagnosis to support I21.4.

discharge_disposition: 63 - Discharged/transferred to a Medicare-certified long-term care hospital (LTCH)

evidence.quote: In the ED the patient met criteria for septic shock with a lactate of 5.1 mmol/L that failed to clear after a 30 mL/kg balanced crystalloid bolus. Given profound hypoxemic respiratory failure and depressed mental status the patient underwent rapid-sequence intubation, and broad-spectrum antimicrobials and vasopressor support were initiated.

Consultation requested by the primary care team. Chart reviewed and patient examined at the bedside. Severe CAP complicated by day-6 VAP. Admission blood cultures grew Streptococcus pneumoniae (now cleared); BAL pending.
Norepinephrine 0.1 mcg/kg/min IV via CVC — titrate to MAP ≥65 mmHg Marcus Bell Administered
Dense left lower lobe consolidation with air bronchograms and developing patchy right basilar airspace opacity.

Discharge / Transfer Diagnoses Resolving sepsis and pneumonia; ventilator-dependent respiratory failure with tracheostomy (weaning); resolved ventilator-associated pneumonia (Pseudomonas); acute kidney injury with renal recovery, hemodialysis discontinued; resolved atrial fibrillation; catheter-associated right IJ DVT on anticoagulation; ICU-acquired weakness; type 2 diabetes; COPD; hypertension; hyperlipidemia.
Interval: fever recrudescence, rising WBC, purulent secretions and new right infiltrate - VAP suspected; antimicrobials broadened per ID
CRRT (CVVHDF) initiation — right femoral dialysis catheter; RCA anticoagulation Marcus Bell Administered
New AF with RVR in the setting of sepsis, catecholamines, and electrolyte shifts; preserved ejection fraction on bedside echo. Likely secondary/reversible.
AKI requiring RRT N17.9 01/08/2026 Resolved Renal recovery day 24; HD DC'd

system_note: Audit summary (claim MR_01): The record supports organism-specific sepsis (A40.3) with septic shock (R65.21), acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (J96.01) and ARDS (J80), and documents ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) due to Pseudomonas that developed after intubation. However, several billed elements are incorrect: J95.851 (ventilator-associated pneumonia) was billed POA=Y and as CC but the chart documents VAP developing during the admission and the VAP policy classifies J95.851 as MCC with POA=N; Z99.2 (dependence on renal dialysis) remains billed despite the medical record stating hemodialysis was discontinued before transfer; I21.4 (NSTEMI) is coded without documentation of a provider diagnosis of NSTEMI. Key supporting citations used below (document / section / page): - Provider admission H&P documents septic shock with lactate 5.1 and immediate intubation (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n9, H&P, p.770) (ev1). - Infectious Diseases consult documents organism identification: admission blood cultures grew Streptococcus pneumoniae (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n50, ID consult, p.139) (ev2). - Physician orders / MAR show vasopressor administration (norepinephrine administered) supporting septic shock (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n520, Orders, p.258) (ev3). - Chest radiograph documents multifocal/lobar consolidation consistent with pneumonia and later progression (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n12, Diagnostic Imaging, p.416) (ev4). - Discharge / Transfer Summary explicitly documents: resolved VAP (Pseudomonas); renal recovery with hemodialysis discontinued; ventilator-dependent respiratory failure with tracheostomy - supporting VAP diagnosis and showing dialysis was stopped prior to transfer (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n829, Discharge/Transfer Summary, p.818) (ev5). - Progress note documents new right infiltrate with purulent secretions and VAP suspected on hospital day 6 (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n49, Critical Care Progress Note, p.139) (ev6). - Physician orders document CRRT initiation (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n520, Orders, p.258) and later notes/Problem List document renal recovery (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n5, Hospital Problem List, p.455) (ev7, ev9). - Cardiology consult documents the atrial arrhythmia as secondary/reversible (NOT diagnostic of NSTEMI) (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n37, Cardiology Consult, p.639) (ev8). - The governing VAP policy explicitly lists J95.851 as Ventilator associated pneumonia [MCC] and requires VAP onset >48 hours after intubation and POA=N (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia.docx-b8) (ev10). Reasoned determinations line-by-line (examples): - A40.3 (Sepsis due to Streptococcus pneumoniae): keep as principal. Supported by ID culture result (ev2) and inpatient sepsis documentation (ev1). - R65.21 (Severe sepsis with septic shock): keep as additional MCC; vasopressors and elevated lactate are documented (ev3, ev1) and the policy requires R65.21 to be reported with organism-specific A40.-/A41.- when criteria are met. - J95.851 (Ventilator-associated pneumonia): keep but correct POA to N and severity to MCC. Provider and ID notes document VAP developing on hospital day 6 with bronchoscopy and targeted therapy (ev6, ev2, ev5); policy requires POA=N and classifies J95.851 as MCC (ev10). The originally-billed POA=Y and CC tier are incorrect. - Z99.2 (Dependence on renal dialysis): remove. The record documents CRRT initiation (ev7) but also documents renal recovery with hemodialysis discontinued prior to transfer (ev9, ev5); dependence on dialysis was not a persistent discharge status and should not remain an active dependence code. - I21.4 (NSTEMI): remove. Cardiology consultation characterizes troponin elevation and atrial arrhythmia as secondary to sepsis/catecholamines and does not diagnose NSTEMI; discharge summary and problem list do not list NSTEMI (ev8, ev5). - 7204 (claim line artifact / not a valid ICD-10 code): remove. This appears to be an invalid/errant claim-line entry and is not reflected in the clinician documentation of active problems (ev5). All kept diagnosis/procedure codes and POA/severity assignments are listed in the revised code sets below with the evidence items supporting each change named in code_decisions. Auditor action: remove invalid code 7204; change POA for J95.851 to N and upgrade its severity to MCC; remove Z99.2 and I21.4. Cite: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n9 (H&P, p.770) (ev1); NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n50 (ID consult, p.139) (ev2); NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n520 (Orders, p.258) (ev3); NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n12 (Imaging, p.416) (ev4); NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n829 (Discharge/Transfer Summary, p.818) (ev5); NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n49 (Progress Note, p.139) (ev6); NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n520 (Orders, p.258) (ev7); NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n37 (Cardiology, p.639) (ev8); NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n5 (Problem List, p.455) (ev9); RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Ventilator-Associated-Pneumonia.docx-b8 (VAP policy) (ev10).
rationale_letter: Re: DRG audit determination - Claim MR_01 Dear Provider/Coding Team, We completed an audit of the inpatient DRG coding for claim MR_01 (admit 2026-01-06 to 2026-04-11). The medical record documents a severe infectious pulmonary presentation with septic shock and respiratory failure requiring intubation, prolonged mechanical ventilation, tracheostomy, CRRT/HD for AKI, and an ICU course complicated by ventilator-associated pneumonia (Pseudomonas). Our findings and the corrections we are making are summarized below. Finding (required correction) 1. Ventilator-associated pneumonia (J95.851) - POA indicator and severity tier incorrect: The chart documents VAP developing on hospital day 6 (ICU progress note: "Interval: fever recrudescence, rising WBC, purulent secretions and new right infiltrate - VAP suspected" and ID consult: "Severe CAP complicated by day-6 VAP") and the discharge summary documents "resolved ventilator-associated pneumonia (Pseudomonas)" (supporting citations: Critical Care Progress Note and ID Consult; Discharge/Transfer Summary). Per the governing VAP policy, J95.851 is a ventilator-associated pneumonia diagnosis (MCC) that requires onset greater than 48 hours after intubation and must be assigned POA = N (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Ventilator-Associated-Pneumonia.docx-b8). The claim originally carried POA=Y and was assigned as CC; we are correcting the POA to N and the severity to MCC. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n49 (Progress Note, p.139); NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n50 (ID consult, p.139); NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n829 (Discharge/Transfer Summary, p.818); RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Ventilator-Associated-Pneumonia.docx-b8. 2. Z99.2 (Dependence on renal dialysis) - removal: Although CRRT/hemodialysis was pursued for sepsis-associated AKI (Physician Orders show CRRT initiation), the discharge documentation and problem list document renal recovery and that hemodialysis was discontinued prior to transfer ("AKI requiring RRT ... Resolved | Renal recovery day 24; HD DC'd" and Discharge Summary: "hemodialysis discontinued"). Dependence on dialysis (Z99.2) should not remain active when dialysis dependence has resolved. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n520 (Orders, p.258); NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n5 (Problem List, p.455); NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n829 (Discharge/Transfer Summary, p.818). 3. I21.4 (NSTEMI) - removal: Cardiology consultation attributes troponin rise and arrhythmia to sepsis/catecholamines and characterizes the arrhythmia as likely secondary/reversible; the cardiology note does not document a diagnosis of NSTEMI and the discharge summary does not list NSTEMI. There is no provider-authored diagnosis of NSTEMI to support I21.4. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n37 (Cardiology Consult, p.639); NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n829 (Discharge Summary, p.818). Other confirmations / no-change items (kept as coded) - A40.3 (Sepsis due to Streptococcus pneumoniae) remains principal (supported by culture documentation: "Admission blood cultures grew Streptococcus pneumoniae (now cleared)") and the treating team's sepsis/septic shock documentation (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n50; n9). Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n50 (ID consult, p.139); NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n9 (H&P, p.770). - R65.21 (Severe sepsis with septic shock) remains additional MCC - vasopressor administration and elevated lactate are documented (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n520; n9). - J96.01 (Acute respiratory failure with hypoxia) and J80 (ARDS) remain coded as MCC - documentation of intubation, ABGs, P/F ratios and radiographic bilateral opacities support these selections (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n9; n12; n28). - Procedures (endotracheal intubation, central/arterial line placement, bronchoscopy with BAL, CRRT/dialysis catheter placement, tracheostomy, PEG, ventilator >96 hours) are supported by the orders and progress notes and are retained as billed (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n520; n49; n829). Correction being made to claim MR_01 - Remove: 7204 (invalid/errant claim line), I21.4, Z99.2 - Keep and correct: J95.851 - set POA = N and severity = MCC - Keep: A40.3 (principal), R65.21, J13, J96.01, J80, N17.9, B96.5, I48.91, F05, G72.81, I82.C11, E11.65, J44.9, I10, E78.5, Z99.11 - Keep all billed procedures as originally submitted (see revised procedure list below) If you disagree with these coding edits (for example, if you have documentation documenting NSTEMI or a continuing dialysis dependence not present in the chart extracts reviewed here), please provide the specific dated provider note(s) that state those diagnoses as active at discharge so we may re-evaluate. Sincerely, Clinical Audit Team Key evidence (document id and page): NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n9 p.770 (H&P); n50 p.139 (ID consult); n520 p.258 (Orders/MAR); n12 p.416 (CXR report); n49 p.139 (ICU progress); n829 p.818 (Discharge/Transfer Summary); n37 p.639 (Cardiology consult); n5 p.455 (Problem List); RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Ventilator-Associated-Pneumonia.docx-b8 (VAP policy).
